sources.name: Yurimanga
sources.description: Small yuri-only fan platform with a ~2007-era table-layout design and no Cloudflare anywhere. Has no series/chapter-list concept at all: each of the 763 real entries in its own /mangalist/ catalog is an independent, standalone old-school multi-page image reader, so this source honestly models each entry as its own single-chapter manga rather than inventing a series layer the site itself doesn't have. Two curated homepage feeds (Most Viewed, Most Viewed 18+) plus the full A-Z catalog, client-side search and an 18+ content filter (the one real flag this site has), full manga details, and full chapter reading that fetches every page individually since page-image filenames aren't a predictable function of the page number.

sources.name: Keikomik
sources.description: Indonesian-language manga/manhwa/manhua platform on Vercel/Next.js, read through its own real JSON API and each page's embedded __NEXT_DATA__ payload rather than scraped markup. No Cloudflare anywhere on the main site. Six sort-based browse feeds each confirmed to genuinely reorder results (two cross-checked against the homepage's own server-rendered Popular/Update sections), a live-scraped 11-entry genre filter, search (a real but prefix-only, 10-result-capped title match), full manga details, and full chapter reading sourced from each detail/chapter page's own complete embedded chapter history rather than its client-side-paginated visible HTML list, which was confirmed live to undercount the real total.

sources.name: BL village
sources.description: Real, server-rendered Astro site (no Cloudflare challenge) hosting two distinct BL catalogs under one URL space: ~12680 untranslated Japanese doujinshi one-shots browsable by the homepage's own paginated catalog or by 359 real fandom categories, and 4725 translated multi-chapter series with a real server-side title search. Doujin page counts are read from each work's embedded astro-island payload rather than the raw HTML, which was confirmed live to server-render only the first 10 pages of every work regardless of its real length. Four browse feeds, title search (plus a fandom-category discovery bonus), full manga details, and full chapter reading for both catalogs.

sources.name: LelManga
sources.description: French-language ('VF') manga/manhwa/manhua platform on the 'mangareader' WordPress theme. Five order-based browse feeds, an 89-entry genre filter, a real WordPress search with reliable pagination, full manga details, and full chapter reading sourced from each chapter page's own embedded ts_reader reader-state JSON. Detail/chapter URLs use a type-specific path (/manga/, /manhwa/ or /manhua/) rather than one fixed prefix, tracked as part of each title's own id. A manga's own chapter list is capped to roughly its most recent chapters for the handful of very long-running series (e.g. only chapters 1009-1191 for a title at 1191), a confirmed site-side limitation.

Six order-based browse feeds, a 70-entry genre filter, search, full manga details (tolerant of the site's own French/English field-label inconsistency across pages), and full chapter reading, with the chapter list fetched from the theme's own ajax/chapters/ endpoint since it is not server-rendered on the detail page.

sources.name: Wattpad
sources.description: Reads Wattpad entirely through its own unauthenticated JSON API, confirmed live end to end with zero Cloudflare/challenge markers on any request, not scraped HTML: /api/v3/stories for the Hot/New/Featured browse feeds with real numeric-category genre filtering (the site's own tag= query param is a confirmed no-op), /v4/search/stories for search, /api/v3/stories/{id} for full details plus its complete inline chapter list, and /apiv2/storytext for chapter prose. Paywalled Paid Stories chapters are detected by their own boilerplate and shown as an honest placeholder instead.

Real paginated search via the same endpoint that powers the site's own search page, an 18-genre feed list, and a live-fetched tag filter. sources.name: MangaPlaza
sources.description: Kodansha/C'moA's official licensed digital manga storefront. Full genre-filtered search/browse across three real sort feeds and a 22-genre catalog, real series details, and the complete real chapter list per title (locked past each title's own free-preview count). A free chapter's real, correctly-ordered page-image URLs are now returned reliably (the CloudFront-signed cookies this needs are forwarded correctly), but actually displaying the pages still needs reversing the site's own SpeedBinB client-side pixel-tile DRM scramble (no canvas primitive available), the same category of limitation as this repo's mangago.me and viz.com sources.

sources.name: Naver Webtoon
sources.description: Naver's own official Korean webtoon platform (the sister site, same company/CDN family, to this repo's webtoons.com source), read through its real server-rendered mobile pages with no Cloudflare challenge and no mobile/desktop UA split needed. Eight real weekday-schedule feeds plus a Completed listing, a 13-entry genre filter, search, full series details, and complete chapter reading via the site's own paginated episode list. Naver's real 19+ account-and-login wall is respected: anonymously, age-restricted titles are dropped from every listing rather than surfaced unopenable, and individually-paywalled recent episodes are listed and clearly marked. Optional: paste your signed-in NID_AUT and NID_SES cookies in the source's settings to list 19+ titles (marked 18+, so your content settings apply) and read episodes your account owns. Not yet confirmed with a real account.

sources.description: MangaToon's own PHP-rendered web reader, real server HTML with no Cloudflare challenge encountered anywhere. sources.name: MangaDex
sources.description: MangaDex's official, fully public JSON API, with no scraping, no bot protection encountered anywhere. Browse (Latest/Most Followed/Top Rated/Recently Added), grouped genre/theme/format/content tag filtering, search, full details, and complete chapter reading via MangaDex's own at-home image CDN (no referer needed, real un-DRM'd images). A small number of chapters on some titles are metadata-only entries pointing at an official publisher's own site (VIZ, MangaPlus) with no page images MangaDex itself can serve. These are left out of the chapter list entirely rather than listed as a dead end. Chapters show in your chosen language (English by default, changeable in the source's settings, or all languages); a title with none in it lists the language it does have instead of showing no chapters, with that language named beside each chapter. Per-title content rating (MangaDex serves everything from all-ages to explicit, correctly tagged) is reflected per manga rather than hiding the whole source.

sources.name: Comix
sources.description: comix.to signs every API request and returns encrypted responses, so this source does not reimplement that crypto. It lets the site's own code sign and decrypt, then reads the plaintext react-query state the site itself produced. Browse feeds (Latest Updates, Most Followed, Trending) and full title details come straight from each page's server-rendered state with no WebView at all; search and chapter lists use the app's native in-page execution, which walks all of a long series' chapter pages inside a single WebView load. The site now scrambles the field names of everything it fetches client-side (search results, chapter lists, a chapter's pages) and may change them on any deploy, so this source recognises each value by what it is (a chapter's own link gives its id and number, a title's link gives its id) and does not depend on any field name. Chapter pages are plain images on a rotating set of hosts that answer only a request with no Referer, and are handed to the reader as they are. The old tile-scrambled pages no longer show up in the site's data; if shuffled pages ever return, that needs a live check. Per-title content rating (comix.to serves everything from all-ages to explicit, correctly tagged) is reflected per manga rather than hiding the whole source. A 500 chapter title (25 pages of the site's own chapter list) no longer waits on the site's own retry of a refused request, which cost 5 to 11 seconds each time it happened inside the app: the walk goes on to the next page, and asks again at once for any page the site is still holding back. Checked against the live site in a real browser: 500 of 500 chapters of a long title, 120 pages of a chapter, and 168 search results all read correctly. Not yet tried inside the Boundless or Sumizuri app itself, because the site's Cloudflare check in a test web view is an interactive one.

sources.name: Kagane
sources.description: Community reader aggregator (many scanlation groups upload to one platform, similar in spirit to MangaDex). The site now lives on four mirror addresses (kagane.si, kagane.cx, kagane.moe and kagane.net; kagane.org only lists them behind a Cloudflare check): this source uses the first one that answers and moves to the next when it stops. Browse feeds, search, details and chapter lists use the site's own JSON API with plain requests, with a call made inside a page of the site as the fallback when the app's own request is refused. A chapter's full page list comes from the site's own reader page, since the request that returns it needs a token only the site's real page code can mint; the images then load from kstatic.to with no Referer. The site's Content and language settings are source settings here: content rating (Safe, 15+ or 18+, default 18+ so the app's own content settings blur or hide each title by its rating) and preferred chapter language (default English, or Any). Genre filters work (several included genres list titles with any of them). Per-title content rating is reflected per manga rather than hiding the whole source. Not yet tried inside the Boundless or Sumizuri app itself: the API, the reader page and the extension's own reader script were run against the live mirrors in a real browser. Titles rated 18+ show an age prompt in the site's reader; this source presses its 'Only this time' button for the reader, and that one step has only been tried against a stand-in page.

sources.name: MangaFire
sources.description: Large aggregator, back up after being down. Not Cloudflare-challenge-gated (a plain request reaches it fine); every real endpoint instead requires a site-issued token only its own page JS can mint, so search, title details, chapter lists, and chapter pages all run through the app's real in-page execution the first time. Those tokens never change for a given URL, so every URL the page produced is remembered and replayed with a plain request afterwards: a title, chapter or volume you have opened before, the Latest Updates pages and repeated searches open without loading the site's page at all. Chapter lists that span more than one page are fetched by paging through the site's own real UI, not truncated to page 1, in the same single visit that returns the title's details. Titles that have volumes also list them (English): the app shows a Chapters / Volumes switch, and each volume reads as one long chapter. Search-result cards don't carry a content rating (the site's own API doesn't return one at that shape); only a title's own details page does, and is reflected per manga rather than hiding the whole source. Two feeds: Trending (a plain request) and Latest Updates (the homepage's fresh chapters list, paged). Not yet timed inside the Boundless app itself: the web view part is measured in a real WKWebView, and the Chapters / Volumes switch needs a Boundless build that has it.

sources.name: ToonGrab
